title: Muse gadget apps API
doc: What a WebAssembly app on a Muse gadget can call, the events it gets and the constants it uses. The firmware embeds its machine-readable projection and serves it in parts with app.api; gen_api.py makes the C header apps include, the reference, and the firmware's import table from it.
conventions: Every function is imported from the module "gadget". An app that imports anything else isn't run.

Integers are 32-bit and signed. Colours are 0xRRGGBB. Opacity runs from 0 (transparent) to 255 (opaque). Angles are whole degrees, clockwise, with 0 at 3 o'clock, as in LVGL. Percentages run from 0 to 100.
Strings are NUL-terminated UTF-8 in the app's memory. A call copies what it needs before it returns.
A handle or id is positive; 0 is never a valid one. A function that can fail returns a negative ERR_ constant.

Nothing blocks. A call that needs the VM, or takes time, returns an operation id at once and finishes later with EV_DONE (a: the id, b: 0 or more on success, or an ERR_). A buffer given to such a call must stay reserved until then.
Changes to the screen made in one callback appear together on the next frame after it returns. Getters see every change made so far.

The gadget describes itself: board facts come from sys_info, and its sensors and other hardware from dev_ calls, each with a description the firmware supplies. device.guide gives Muse the same before it writes an app.

coord.doc: Pixels, PCT(p) of the parent, or SIZE_CONTENT.

handle.doc: A UI object, style, canvas or sensor this app made: positive.

op.doc: An operation id (positive) that EV_DONE finishes, or an ERR_.

result.doc: 0 or more on success, or an ERR_.

text.doc: Used only by properties: set with ui_set_text, read with ui_get_text.

bytes.doc: Bytes in the app's memory, and their length.

out.doc: A buffer in the app's memory, and its size in bytes.

values: The app's screen: the parent of top-level objects. It can't be deleted.
A width or height that fits the object's content.
p percent (0 to 1000) of the parent's content area.
A radius that makes the object round, or its ends fully rounded.
What ui_get returns for a wrong handle or property; the log says which.
limits: The most memory one app takes: its linear memory and stack, and what the firmware holds for it (objects, styles, canvases, images, chat text, device queues). Gadgets give each app this much, or less where PSRAM is short (never under 1 MB): device.guide capabilities.wasm.budget_kb and sys_info(INFO_MEM_BUDGET) say how much.
Instructions per callback, well under a second. Past that the app traps and stops.
UI objects alive at once, the root included.
Operations in flight (VM reads and writes, chat sends, image loads).
Readings kept per open device; the oldest are dropped past that.
Chat messages kept for the app.
Text kept per chat message; longer messages are cut and marked.
A text property or string argument.
All of one app's state files on the VM.
One sys_log line; longer ones are cut.
Decoded images and canvases together: no more pixels than the screen has (0 here means the screen's own count).
on_frame calls per second, at most.
An object's position, width and height in pixels, either way; larger values are clamped.
Shadow width, spread and offsets, line dashes, and radii other than RADIUS_CIRCLE; larger values are clamped.
The app's styles on one object: shared ones from ui_style_add plus each selector ui_style sets; past that ERR_LIMIT.

exports.name: on_start
exports.doc: Called once the app is loaded: build the screen here.

exports.name: on_event
exports.doc: Called for each event (EV_ constants; the table under Events says what a and b hold).

exports.name: on_frame
exports.doc: Called up to sys_frame_rate times a second while the screen is on, with sys_millis(). Leave it out unless the app animates something itself: widgets, animations and timers don't need it.

exports.name: on_stop
exports.doc: Called before the app is closed, unless it trapped. Save state here: state_save calls made in on_stop finish (for up to 2 s) before the app's memory is freed.

events: Something happened to an object the app asked about with ui_on, or an image load finished.
A touch began on the root, or on an object that isn't clickable.
An operation finished: b is 0 or more on success (bytes read, say), or an ERR_.
Readings to take with dev_take, after dev_open. At most one per frame per device.
A device's event (dev_event gives the index), after dev_open.
The screen went off (on_frame stops) or came back.
The link to the VM came up or went down.

enums.name: error
enums.doc: Why a call failed. Every one is negative.
values: An argument is out of range, a string is too long, or a buffer lies outside the app's memory.
The handle or id isn't one this app holds, or is the wrong kind for the call.
The app's memory budget is used up.
A per-app limit was reached (objects, styles, timers, operations, open sensors).
The thing is in use; try again later.
The gadget isn't connected to its VM.
The app's manifest doesn't ask for this permission, or the VM refused.
This gadget doesn't have it: a sensor, an output, or a property on this widget.
The data is larger than the call takes.
The file, state or message doesn't exist.
The VM didn't answer in time.
Anything else; the app's log says why.

enums.name: info
values: The API version the gadget serves, major * 100 + minor.
Pixels to keep clear of the edges so nothing is cut off: on a round screen, the inset of the largest centred square.
The buttons this gadget reports, as bits: 1 << BUTTON_x.
1 if the gadget has a knob or wheel (EV_KNOB).
The app's memory budget in bytes: limits.budget_bytes, or less on a gadget short of PSRAM.
Bytes of the budget in use.
1 while the gadget is connected to its VM.

enums.name: stop
enums.doc: Why an app is being closed (on_stop).
values: The person closed it (the power key, or the exit button held 2 s) or Muse ran app.stop.
The gadget is restarting, for an update or a setting.

enums.name: button
enums.doc: Buttons, by role. Which exist depends on the board (INFO_BUTTONS). The power key always closes the app and is never reported. Holding BUTTON_PRIMARY (the talk button) for 2 s closes it too: device.guide names it as exit_hold; the app sees its BTN_DOWN and BTN_LONG, then on_stop, and never its BTN_UP. If the app gives the talk button back to Muse with muse_talk_key(1), that hold is reserved for talking instead; provide an on-screen Close control or use app.stop.
values: The talk button. Muse's push-to-talk while muse_talk_key(1).
The second button, where the board has one.

enums.name: button_action
values: Still held 600 ms after DOWN; UP still follows.

enums.name: muse_mode
values: Something failed; the caption says what.

enums.name: chat_event
enums.doc: What changed in the chat (EV_CHAT's a).
values: A new message; b is its id.
A message's text grew while Muse writes it; b is its id.
A message is complete; b is its id.
b is 1 while Muse is working on a reply, 0 once it's idle.
b is 1 once the chat is followed, 0 when the link is lost (it reconnects by itself).

enums.name: chat_info
enums.doc: What chat_info reports about a message.
values: 1 if the text was cut to chat_text_bytes.

enums.name: chat_role
values: An app on a gadget, with chat_send. Its "[name on the gadget]" prefix is removed.

groups: Time, logging, board facts, timers and the app's own lifecycle.

LVGL widgets, kept by the firmware. Create them once, change their properties, and ask for their events with ui_on. Properties are P_ constants (Properties, below); style properties set this way apply to the main part in the default state.
Style properties for other parts and states, and shared styles.
Animating a property to a value.
Immediate-mode drawing on a canvas object (W_CANVAS). Drawing shows on the next frame.
What Muse is doing, and the talk key.
Following the chat and sending to it, through the gadget's link to the VM. The gadget parses the VM's formats; the app sees messages.

Reading files on the VM (the app's own folder, or the home folder with the files.home permission) and the gadget's own files on its flash, which Muse puts there with files.put (paths from "/", with the files.gadget permission).
Small files the app keeps between runs, on the VM under the gadget's folder (devices/<gadget>/state/<app>/).

Sensors, motors, relays and anything else the firmware has a driver for. The firmware describes each device: a name, its readings (fields with units), its actions (with their parameters) and its events. Apps find devices by name and read, stream or call them through these few functions, so new hardware needs no new imports and no change to this file. Well-known names (Devices, below) have fixed fields and units so apps work across boards; any other name carries its own description.

functions.name: sys_millis
functions.doc: A clock for timing. Wraps after 24 days.

functions.name: sys_time
functions.doc: The time of day. 0 until the gadget has set its clock from the VM, soon after it connects.

functions.name: sys_log
functions.doc: Adds a line to the app's log, which Muse reads with app.logs.

functions.name: sys_info
functions.doc: Board facts and the app's memory use.

functions.name: sys_random
functions.doc: From the hardware random number generator.

functions.name: sys_timer
functions.doc: Starts or restarts a timer: EV_TIMER after ms milliseconds, while the app runs, screen on or off.

functions.name: sys_timer_stop
functions.doc: Stops a timer.

functions.name: sys_frame_rate
functions.doc: How often on_frame is called while the screen is on. 30 to start with, if the app exports on_frame.

functions.name: sys_keep_awake
functions.doc: Keeps the screen on while on is 1. Use it only while showing something the person is watching.

functions.name: sys_exit
functions.doc: Ends the app once the current callback returns, after on_stop(STOP_EXIT).

functions.name: sys_brightness
args: 1 to 100, or -1 for the person's own setting.
functions.doc: Sets the screen's brightness while the app runs.

functions.name: ui_create
args: UI_ROOT, or another object other than a roller.
functions.doc: Creates a widget with the theme's look.

functions.name: ui_delete
functions.doc: Deletes an object and its children. Their handles become invalid.

functions.name: ui_clean
functions.doc: Deletes an object's children.

functions.name: ui_set
functions.doc: Sets a property that isn't text.

functions.name: ui_get
functions.doc: Reads a property that isn't text.

functions.name: ui_set_text
functions.doc: Sets a text property.

functions.name: ui_get_text
args: Gets the text, cut to fit and always NUL-terminated.
ret: The text's full length in bytes.
functions.doc: Reads a text property, such as what was typed into a text area.

functions.name: ui_on
functions.doc: Chooses which events of this object come to on_event as EV_UI. Replaces the earlier choice.

functions.name: ui_align
functions.doc: Places an object in its parent, offset by dx, dy.

functions.name: ui_align_to
functions.doc: Places an object relative to another, once (it doesn't follow base later).

functions.name: ui_set_parent
args: Not a roller, nor the object or one inside it.
functions.doc: Moves an object to another parent.

functions.name: ui_grid
functions.doc: Lays out the object's children in a grid. Sizes are space-separated: pixels, "auto" (fits the content) or "Nfr" (N shares of what's left), up to 8 each: ui_grid(obj, "1fr 1fr 1fr", "auto 1fr"). Place children with ui_grid_cell.

functions.name: ui_grid_cell
functions.doc: Puts a child in a grid cell; the child stretches to fill it.

functions.name: ui_scroll_to
functions.doc: Scrolls an object's content.

functions.name: ui_scroll_to_view
functions.doc: Scrolls its parents until the object is visible: the newest message in a chat, say.

functions.name: ui_navigation
functions.doc: On boards without touch: buttons and the knob move focus between the app's buttons, sliders and other inputs (UP and DOWN, or the knob), ENTER presses or edits, BACK sends UI_CANCEL. Buttons it uses don't come as EV_BUTTON while it's on.

functions.name: ui_text_width
functions.doc: How wide a line of text is.

functions.name: ui_text_height
functions.doc: How tall text is, wrapped at width.

functions.name: ui_span
args: Pixels to keep clear at each end.
ret: Pixels, centred on the screen; 0 off the screen.
functions.doc: How much of row y shows, less margin at each end: on a round screen the circle's chord, else the screen's width. Size text and rows near the top and bottom of a round screen by it.

functions.name: ui_fit_text
functions.doc: Fits a label's text on one line width wide: in font, or the next smaller font it fits in, down to FONT_14, then cut short with "...". Sets the label's width, font and long mode. Call it after ui_set_text, and again when the text changes, for any text whose length you don't control: a name, a message, a number that can grow.

functions.name: ui_image_load
args: In the app's folder on the VM, or from "/" on the gadget (files.gadget).
functions.doc: Loads a PNG or JPEG into an image object, from the VM or from the gadget's own files (which work offline). EV_UI with UI_LOADED or UI_LOAD_FAILED says when it's done. The decoded image counts against the budget.

functions.name: ui_image_set
functions.doc: Shows a PNG or JPEG from the app's memory, decoded at once.

functions.name: ui_line_points
functions.doc: Sets a line's points.

functions.name: ui_chart_series
functions.doc: Adds a series to a chart.

functions.name: ui_chart_set
functions.doc: Sets a series' points.

functions.name: ui_chart_push
functions.doc: Adds a point to a series, as P_UPDATE_MODE says.

functions.name: ui_table_cell
functions.doc: Sets a cell's text, adding rows and columns as needed.

functions.name: ui_scale_needle
args: A line object, child of the scale.
functions.doc: Points a line at a value on a round scale.

functions.name: ui_style
functions.doc: Sets a style property for one part and state: ui_style(slider, PART_INDICATOR, P_BG_COLOR, 0x00C8FF). Each selector counts once toward limits.styles_per_object.

functions.name: ui_style_create
functions.doc: Creates a shared style, to give many objects the same look with one set of calls.

functions.name: ui_style_set
functions.doc: Sets a property in a shared style. Objects using it update.

functions.name: ui_style_add
functions.doc: Gives an object a shared style. With the selectors ui_style has set on it, 32 per object (limits.styles_per_object). Properties set on the object itself still win.

functions.name: ui_animate
functions.doc: Animates a property from its value now to to. UI_ANIM_DONE follows, if asked for with ui_on. A new animation of the same property replaces the old one.

functions.name: ui_animate_stop
functions.doc: Stops animations where they are.

functions.name: cv_fill
functions.doc: Fills the whole canvas.

functions.name: cv_opa
functions.doc: Opacity for the drawing calls that follow on this canvas. Starts at OPA_COVER.

functions.name: cv_rect
functions.doc: A filled rectangle; with radius RADIUS_CIRCLE, a circle or pill.

functions.name: cv_rect_style
args: Positive pixels, no wider than the canvas.
Positive pixels, no taller than the canvas.
A shared style from ui_style_create, painted as it is now.
functions.doc: Draws a rectangle with a shared style: P_RADIUS; P_BG_COLOR, P_BG_OPA, P_BG_GRAD_COLOR and P_BG_GRAD_DIR (GRAD_HOR or GRAD_VER, two colour stops); P_BORDER_COLOR, P_BORDER_WIDTH, P_BORDER_OPA and P_BORDER_SIDE; P_SHADOW_COLOR, P_SHADOW_WIDTH, P_SHADOW_OPA, P_SHADOW_OFFSET_X, P_SHADOW_OFFSET_Y and P_SHADOW_SPREAD. P_OPA and cv_opa multiply the fill, border and shadow opacities. Missing properties give a white fill, square corners and no border or shadow. Other properties are ignored. Border and shadow widths are clamped to 0..64 px, shadow spread to 0..64, and offsets to -4096..4096. Drawing, including shadows, is clipped to the canvas buffer: leave room around the rectangle. It paints once; later style changes affect only later calls, not already drawn pixels. No buffer yet means no drawing. Available since API 1.1.

functions.name: cv_border
functions.doc: A rectangle's outline, width pixels thick, inside it.

functions.name: cv_line
functions.doc: A line with round ends.

functions.name: cv_arc
functions.doc: An arc, clockwise from start to end.

functions.name: cv_triangle
functions.doc: A filled triangle.

functions.name: cv_text
args: The top of the first line.
functions.doc: Text, wrapped at w.

functions.name: cv_pixels
args: w * h RGB565 pixels, row by row, little-endian.
functions.doc: Copies pixels in, clipped to the canvas.

functions.name: muse_mode
functions.doc: What Muse is doing now; EV_MUSE says when it changes.

functions.name: muse_caption
functions.doc: The caption the face would show: what Muse heard, or an error.

functions.name: muse_talk_key
functions.doc: With 1, the talk button is Muse's push-to-talk again, as outside apps, and its presses don't come as EV_BUTTON. Off when the app starts.

functions.name: chat_open
functions.doc: Starts following the chat: fetches the latest message, then reports new ones as EV_CHAT. The gadget reconnects by itself.

functions.name: chat_close
functions.doc: Stops following the chat and frees its messages.

functions.name: chat_latest
args: 0 for the newest, 1 for the one before...
ret: A message id, or 0 if there's no such message.
functions.doc: The app keeps the last chat_messages messages.

functions.name: chat_info
functions.doc: About a message.

functions.name: chat_text
args: Gets the text from offset, cut to fit and NUL-terminated.
ret: Bytes copied, not counting the NUL.
functions.doc: A message's text, without attachments or markup the gadget can't show.

functions.name: chat_send
functions.doc: Sends a message to Muse, as "[<app> on the gadget] text". EV_DONE when the VM has it; the reply comes through chat_open.

functions.name: file_read
args: Relative to the app's folder, from "~/" for the home folder (files.home), or from "/" for the gadget's own files (files.gadget).
Gets the bytes; keep it reserved until EV_DONE.
functions.doc: Reads part of a file on the VM, or on the gadget itself (a path from "/"). EV_DONE's b is the bytes read, 0 at the end of the file, or ERR_NOT_FOUND.

functions.name: state_save
functions.doc: Saves a state file on the VM, replacing the last one whole. EV_DONE when it's written.

functions.name: state_load
functions.doc: Loads a state file. EV_DONE's b is its size, or ERR_NOT_FOUND.

functions.name: dev_count
ret: How many devices this gadget has.
functions.doc: With dev_name, lists them all.

functions.name: dev_name
functions.doc: A device's name, by position.

functions.name: dev_find
args: A well-known name (DEV_ constants) or one the gadget lists.
functions.doc: Finds a device by name. ERR_DENIED if the app's manifest names it in neither requires nor uses.

functions.name: dev_describe
args: Gets the description as JSON, cut to fit and NUL-terminated.
functions.doc: The device's description, as device.guide gives it (Devices, below). Apps written for one device rarely need it: Muse already read it.

functions.name: dev_field
ret: The field's index in a reading's values.
functions.doc: Where a field is in a reading.

functions.name: dev_read
functions.doc: The latest reading, without opening the device. ERR_NOT_FOUND until there is one: a sensor that streams starts on the first dev_read (taking a moment), and runs until the app stops or calls dev_close. Its t_ms says how fresh it is. To get every reading, use dev_open and dev_take instead.

functions.name: dev_open
args: Up to the device's rate; 0 for events only.
functions.doc: Starts streaming readings into a queue, and the device's events. EV_DEV_DATA says when readings wait, EV_DEV_EVENT brings events. Close it once the app stops needing it: a running sensor costs battery.

functions.name: dev_take
functions.doc: Takes waiting readings off the queue.

functions.name: dev_close
functions.doc: Stops streaming and events.

functions.name: dev_action
functions.doc: Finds an action by name.

functions.name: dev_call
args: float parameters, in the order the description gives.
For actions that take text; "" otherwise.
functions.doc: Runs an action. It doesn't block: a driver whose action takes time starts it and returns.

functions.name: dev_event
ret: The event's index, as EV_DEV_EVENT gives it.
functions.doc: Finds an event by name.

structs.name: gadget_reading_t
fields: The values, in the order and units of the device's fields.

ui_enums.name: ui_event
ui_enums.doc: Object events, as bits for ui_on; EV_UI's b holds one.
values: Pressed and released without sliding off.
The person changed its value, selection, checked state or text.
A keyboard's OK, or Enter in a one-line text area.
A keyboard's close key, or BACK while navigating.
An animation on the object finished.
ui_image_load failed; the log says why. Sent without ui_on.

ui_enums.name: part
ui_enums.doc: Parts of a widget, for ui_style and ui_style_add. Combine with a STATE_.
values: A bar's, slider's or arc's filled part, a checkbox's box, a scale's major ticks.
A slider's, arc's or switch's handle.
A table's cells, a chart's series, a scale's minor ticks, a keyboard's keys.
A text area's cursor, a chart's cursor.

ui_enums.name: state
values: A slider or roller being changed with keys.

ui_enums.name: align
ui_enums.doc: Where to put an object, as in LVGL.

ui_enums.name: font
ui_enums.doc: The fonts every gadget has: Montserrat, with LVGL's symbols (SYM_).
values: Digits, ':', '.', '-', '%' and the degree sign only.

ui_enums.name: layout
values: Children are placed by x, y and align.
Children flow in rows or columns (P_FLEX_*).

ui_enums.name: place
ui_enums.doc: How flex places items and tracks.

ui_enums.name: long_mode
ui_enums.doc: What a label does with text that doesn't fit its size.

ui_enums.name: image_align
ui_enums.doc: How an image fills an image object larger or smaller than itself.

ui_enums.name: anim_flag
values: Runs back to the start after each run.

widgets: A plain container: a box with a background, border and children.
A container that presses; put a label in it.
A PNG (8-bit channels) or JPEG (baseline) (ui_image_load, ui_image_set).
A ring with a value, which touch can drag.
A bar with a knob to drag.
An on/off toggle; P_CHECKED is its state.
A box with a label; P_CHECKED is its state.
A drum of options to spin.
A button that opens a list of options.
An on-screen keyboard that types into a text area.
Ticks and labels in a line or a dial; ui_scale_needle points a line at a value.
Line or bar series (ui_chart_series, ui_chart_set, ui_chart_push).
Pixels to draw on with the cv_ calls. Its buffer is RGB565 and counts against the budget; P_WIDTH and P_HEIGHT size it, up to the screen.
props: Left edge, from the parent's content area, or the offset from P_ALIGN.
Top edge, or the offset from P_ALIGN.
Where in the parent; P_X and P_Y offset it.
Not drawn, and takes no input or space in a layout.
Takes touch. On for buttons and inputs, off for labels and images.
Scrolls when its content is larger. On for containers.
Its events also go to its parent (one ui_on on a list instead of one per row).
Left out of the parent's layout and scrolling.
The checked state: a switch's or checkbox's value.
Which part of a child to stop on after a horizontal scroll.
How far it's scrolled; scroll with ui_scroll_to.
Its place among its siblings, which sets the drawing order: 0 is drawn first, -1 moves it last.
Across the flow, within a track (see flex_track_place).

Where the tracks sit across the flow. A row or column that doesn't wrap is one track, as wide (or tall) as its largest item, so centring its items across the flow takes PLACE_CENTER here and in flex_cross_place.
A child's share of the free space in its parent's flex track; 0 keeps its own size.
Gap between the object and its outline.
Blur width, 0 to 64. Shadows cost drawing time; use them on a few objects.
Corner radius, 0 to 64; RADIUS_CIRCLE for round.
Gap between rows of a layout.
Gap between columns of a layout.
Tints an image (or a symbol drawn as one).
The whole object and its children.
Rotates the drawn object about its pivot. Costs drawing time and memory.
Scales the drawn object about its pivot.
Moves the drawn object without moving it in the layout.
A scale's tick length (PART_INDICATOR major, PART_ITEMS minor).
Clips children to the rounded corners.
Milliseconds for a widget's own animations: a label's scrolling, a roller's spin.
The text. On a dropdown, fixed text to show in place of the selected option.
The range's low end; a chart's Y axis.
The low end in BAR_RANGE mode.
The indicator's start; setting P_VALUE moves it too.
Spins round instead of stopping at the ends. ERR_ARG if letter spacing leaves its options no height.
The text area it types into.
Every nth tick is major and labelled.
Shifts the picture inside the object, wrapping round.
Y points up from the bottom.

devices.doc: What the firmware says about each device, in device.guide and from dev_describe, as JSON. A driver registers its device with this description; nothing here lists the devices a gadget has.
descriptor: a-z, 0-9 and '_', unique on the gadget. A well-known name when the device is one, so apps for it work unchanged; otherwise the driver's own.
What it is and where it sits, for Muse: "Soil moisture probe on the Grove port".
Its readings' values, in order: {"name", "unit", "min", "max"}. Up to 8; none for a device that only acts.
The highest rate dev_open takes, in Hz; 0 when it's only read on demand (dev_read).
What it does: {"name", "desc", "params": [{"name", "unit", "min", "max"}], "text": true if it takes text}.
Names of what it reports by itself ("tap", "door_open"), in EV_DEV_EVENT's order.

example.name: soil_moisture
example.desc: Capacitive soil moisture probe on the Grove port

well_known: Volatile organic compounds, as Sensirion's VOC index (1 to 500).
Acceleration in the screen's frame: x right, y up, z out of the screen. Events from the IMU's own feature engine where it has one.
Steps counted since dev_open, from the IMU's step counter.
charging and usb are 0 or 1; volts is 0 where the board can't measure it.
Buzzes; a new buzz replaces one still running.
Beeps on the gadget's speaker; ERR_BUSY while Muse listens or speaks.

manifest.doc: A JSON object in the custom section gadget.manifest of the .wasm, which GADGET_MANIFEST() in gadget.h writes from one string literal. The gadget reads it before running the app.
fields: The API version the app was written for, "1.0". A gadget serving an older minor version, or another major one, refuses the app.
The app's folder name under ~/workspace/gadgets/apps/: a-z, 0-9 and '-'.
A name for people: the gadget's launcher shows it under the app's icon.

Its glyph in the gadget's launcher, on a coloured disc: one of timer, clock, calendar, check, list, note, chat, mic, music, heart, pulse, moon, sun, cloud, drop, leaf, bolt, star, spark, smile, game, dice, target, bricks, book, chart, compass, globe, cup, bell, home, pin, camera, flag, wind. Without one the launcher shows the title's first letter.

Permissions, and device names it uses when they're there. A device in neither list can't be found (ERR_DENIED).
features: UP, DOWN, ENTER and BACK, or a knob.
permissions: Follow the chat (chat_open and the other chat_ reads).
Read files outside the app's own folder (file_read with "~/").
Read the gadget's own files (file_read and ui_image_load with a path from "/").
